From 803482f472ccc9576c0e606143725d1d8c61019d Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Isaku Yamahata <isaku.yamahata@intel.com>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2024 17:04:22 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] KVM: x86/mmu: Use SHADOW_NONPRESENT_VALUE for atomic zap in
 TDP MMU

Use SHADOW_NONPRESENT_VALUE when zapping TDP MMU SPTEs with mmu_lock held
for read, tdp_mmu_zap_spte_atomic() was simply missed during the initial
development.

Fixes: 7f01cab84928 ("KVM: x86/mmu: Allow non-zero value for non-present SPTE and removed SPTE")
Signed-off-by: Isaku Yamahata <isaku.yamahata@intel.com>
[sean: write changelog]
Signed-off-by: Sean Christopherson <seanjc@google.com>
Reviewed-by: Kai Huang <kai.huang@intel.com>
Message-ID: <20240518000430.1118488-2-seanjc@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com>

diff --git a/arch/x86/kvm/mmu/tdp_mmu.c b/arch/x86/kvm/mmu/tdp_mmu.c
index 1259dd63defc..36539c1b36cd 100644
--- a/arch/x86/kvm/mmu/tdp_mmu.c
+++ b/arch/x86/kvm/mmu/tdp_mmu.c
@@ -626,7 +626,7 @@ static inline int tdp_mmu_zap_spte_atomic(struct kvm *kvm,
 	 * SPTEs.
 	 */
 	handle_changed_spte(kvm, iter->as_id, iter->gfn, iter->old_spte,
-			    0, iter->level, true);
+			    SHADOW_NONPRESENT_VALUE, iter->level, true);
 
 	return 0;
 }
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/x86/kvm/mmu/tdp_mmu.c`**
   - The function `tdp_mmu_zap_spte_atomic` was modified to replace the second argument of the `handle_changed_spte` function call from `0` to `SHADOW_NONPRESENT_VALUE`. This change ensures that when zapping TDP MMU SPTEs with the `mmu_lock` held for read, the correct non-present value is used.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `tdp_mmu.c` addresses a previously missed implementation detail during the initial development of the TDP MMU. By using `SHADOW_NONPRESENT_VALUE`, the patch corrects the behavior of the atomic zap operation, ensuring it aligns with the intended functionality of handling non-present SPTEs. This change is directly related to the fix for the bug introduced in commit `7f01cab84928`, which allowed for non-zero values for non-present SPTEs.

KVM: x86/mmu: Use SHADOW_NONPRESENT_VALUE for atomic zap in
 TDP MMU

Use SHADOW_NONPRESENT_VALUE when zapping TDP MMU SPTEs with mmu_lock held
for read, tdp_mmu_zap_spte_atomic() was simply missed during the initial
development.

Fixes: 7f01cab84928 ("KVM: x86/mmu: Allow non-zero value for non-present SPTE and removed SPTE")
Signed-off-by: Isaku Yamahata <isaku.yamahata@intel.com>
[sean: write changelog]
Signed-off-by: Sean Christopherson <seanjc@google.com>
Reviewed-by: Kai Huang <kai.huang@intel.com>
Message-ID: <20240518000430.1118488-2-seanjc@google.com>
Signed-off-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the failure to use the correct non-present value (`SHADOW_NONPRESENT_VALUE`) when zapping TDP MMU SPTEs in the `tdp_mmu_zap_spte_atomic` function. Instead, a default value of `0` was used, which did not align with the intended handling of non-present SPTEs, leading to incorrect behavior in the memory management unit.

Here is the patch:
 
 static inline int tdp_mmu_zap_spte_atomic(struct kvm *kvm,
 					  struct tdp_iter *iter)
 {
 	int ret;
 
 	lockdep_assert_held_read(&kvm->mmu_lock);
 
 	/*
 	 * Freeze the SPTE by setting it to a special, non-present value. This
 	 * will stop other threads from immediately installing a present entry
 	 * in its place before the TLBs are flushed.
 	 *
 	 * Delay processing of the zapped SPTE until after TLBs are flushed and
 	 * the REMOVED_SPTE is replaced (see below).
 	 */
 	ret = __tdp_mmu_set_spte_atomic(iter, REMOVED_SPTE);
 	if (ret)
 		return ret;
 
 	kvm_flush_remote_tlbs_gfn(kvm, iter->gfn, iter->level);
 
 	/*
 	 * No other thread can overwrite the removed SPTE as they must either
 	 * wait on the MMU lock or use tdp_mmu_set_spte_atomic() which will not
 	 * overwrite the special removed SPTE value. Use the raw write helper to
 	 * avoid an unnecessary check on volatile bits.
 	 */
 	__kvm_tdp_mmu_write_spte(iter->sptep, SHADOW_NONPRESENT_VALUE);
 
 	/*
 	 * Process the zapped SPTE after flushing TLBs, and after replacing
 	 * REMOVED_SPTE with 0. This minimizes the amount of time vCPUs are
 	 * blocked by the REMOVED_SPTE and reduces contention on the child
 	 * SPTEs.
 	 */
 	handle_changed_spte(kvm, iter->as_id, iter->gfn, iter->old_spte,
-			    0, iter->level, true);
+			    SHADOW_NONPRESENT_VALUE, iter->level, true);
 
 	return 0;
 }

Reason:
The bug occurs because the `tdp_mmu_zap_spte_atomic` function incorrectly uses a default value of `0` when zapping TDP MMU SPTEs instead of the intended `SHADOW_NONPRESENT_VALUE`. This leads to improper handling of non-present SPTEs, which can cause incorrect behavior in the memory management unit.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
__kvm_tdp_mmu_write_spte(iter->sptep, SHADOW_NONPRESENT_VALUE);
handle_changed_spte(kvm, iter->as_id, iter->gfn, iter->old_spte,
                    SHADOW_NONPRESENT_VALUE, iter->level, true);
```
Reason:
The fix involves replacing the incorrect usage of `0` with `SHADOW_NONPRESENT_VALUE` in both the `__kvm_tdp_mmu_write_spte` and `handle_changed_spte` functions. This ensures that the non-present SPTEs are handled correctly, aligning with the intended memory management behavior and preventing potential issues with memory access.
